## 9a. Selected delayed Weber adaptation

This section freezes exactly one comparison selected by the operator on 2026-10-05. It moves the Section 9 bracket onto the ordinary causal roots of Section 1 and differentiates each delayed range along reception time. It retains the transmitter weight, with $\lambda_{\mathrm W}=-1/2$, $\mu_{\mathrm W}=1$, $K_{ij}=K=1$, $c_f=1$, all positive-delay self roots admitted, no boundary response and no softening. It does not retain instantaneous equal-and-opposite partner coupling. The unrestricted speed domain is selected for the screen; strict and inclusive labels apply only where the actual history obeys them. Nothing is adopted into canon.

For every locally smooth ordinary root $S=S_{ij}(T)\in\mathcal C_{ij}(T)$ define $\mathscr R_{ij}(T)=R_{ij}(T,S_{ij}(T))$ and dots as total absolute-reception-time derivatives of this scalar. The frozen law is

$$
\boxed{\mathbf A_i(T)=\sum_j\sum_{S\in\mathcal C_{ij}(T)}\frac{\sigma_{ij}Kc_f}{\mathscr R_{ij}^{,2}|D_{t,ij}|}\left[1-\frac{\dot{\mathscr R}_{ij}^{,2}}{2c_f^2}+\frac{\mathscr R_{ij}\ddot{\mathscr R}_{ij}}{c_f^2}\right]\mathbf n_{ij}.}
$$

The same-time endpoint is excluded. The domain consists of $C^2$ receiver and transmitter histories with positive range, isolated roots, $D_t\ne0$, a finite root census (or a separately proved absolutely convergent sum), and an invertible present-acceleration matrix. Folds, coincident hits and accumulation are outside this first screen; no cancelling divergent contributions or root exclusions supply a continuation.

Let $D_r=c_f-\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf V_i(T)$, $p=S'=D_r/D_t$, $\mathbf w=\mathbf V_i-p\mathbf V_j(S)$ and $\mathbf w_\perp=(I-\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T})\mathbf w$. Differentiation of the arrival identity gives

$$
\dot{\mathscr R}=c_f(1-p),\qquad
\ddot{\mathscr R}=\frac{c_f}{D_t}\left[\mathbf n\cdot(\mathbf A_i(T)-p^2\mathbf A_j(S))+\frac{\|\mathbf w_\perp\|^2}{\mathscr R}\right].
$$

The second derivative therefore contains both present receiver acceleration and delayed transmitter acceleration, even for self hits. The present unknown lies in the block $M_i=I-\sum_{j,S}\sigma_{ij}K\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T}/(\mathscr R|D_t|D_t)$; delayed accelerations are supplied by the history. This is a neutral delayed implicit law. The instantaneous pair denominators of Section 9 are inapplicable. An undefined self hit or singular $M_i$ is a bounded obstruction for this specification.

The instantaneous invariants are not premises. Time translation, common spatial translation and rotation remain symmetries of this delay law, but no local Lagrangian or conserved energy-like function follows from those symmetries alone. Generic hit directions do not lie on present pair-separation lines; reciprocal hits occur at different emissions, so the instantaneous sum-of-velocities, angular-momentum and pair radial-energy proofs do not survive. A closed-form common-velocity affine control already shows loss of Galilean boost invariance. No nontrivial instantaneous invariant is established for this adaptation. The [pair controls](../binary-research/analysis/weber-delayed-pair-controls.md) and [first ring screen](../braid-program/analysis/weber-delayed-ring-screen.md) develop only this frozen law. Any other reading of a delayed Weber bracket is a separate selection.
